newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bills ease, shares mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bills ease, shares mixed in thin trade.

text.p: A few Russian shares firmed in thin trade over Christmas on Wednesday and Thursday, working days in Russia, and banks sold Treasury bills to raise money to pay end-of-year bills, dealers said on Thursday.
Shares of leading oil company LUKoil outperformed a quiet market, rising to $10.77 from $10.10 at Wednesday's close.
The Russian Trading System index dropped less than one percent on an extremely low $2.2 million turnover.

Anton Kudryashov, head of equity trading at Renaissance Capital, attributed LUKoil's rise to an unconfirmed report of the company's nine-month results, the impact of which was exaggerated in thin trade.
Foreign investors who had snapped up Russian shares before Christmas holidays, fearing to miss a market rise seen in early January, stayed at home over Christmas, he said.
Norilsk Nickel rose to $5.32 from $5.27, Rostelekom was at $2.385 after $2.370, UES fell to $0.0865 from $0.0866 and Mosenergo was unchanged at $0.978.
Prices of Treasury bills and government bonds fell as banks sold paper to support liquidity -- a move backed by speculators, dealers said.
"At the end of the year, many find themselves with unplanned bills," said Konstantin Demchenko of Natsionaly Reservny Bank.
An average six-month bill maturing in April 1997, issue 22055, fell to 89.50 from 90.22 on Tuesday.
The rouble market did not show sharp demand for the currency, however, and was marked by only a few trades, dealers said.
Tomorrow roubles edged down to 5,561-62 per dollar from 5,558-59 on Wednesday.
Speculators were seen ignoring the rouble market through the end of long Russian holidays, up to Russian Orthodox Christmas on January 7 or Orthodox New Year on January 13.
"Speculative trading is not attractive now as the market is too thin," said Interbank Finance House chief dealer Mikhail Kulinich.
Overnight credits fell to 15-25 percent from 20-30 percent on Wednesday.
